title: Hypercohomology filtrations
statement:
Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y'\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g':X'\to X$. Let $K\in\Dplus(X_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories] have torsion cohomology (the construction below does not use this hypothesis) and choose $a$ with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$. Represent $K$ by a complex $K^\bullet$ of abelian sheaves with $K^i=0$ for $i<a$ [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], and let $\tau_{\leq q}K^\bullet$ be its canonical truncations, with the truncation triangles $\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K\to\mathcal H^q(K)[-q]\to$ of [def-sp-truncation-couple]. Pages are indexed as in [def-sp-exact-couple]: the first page of the spectral sequence of a couple is $E_2=E$.

1. **The first truncation spectral sequence (on $Y$).** $(D,E)$ is the truncation couple [def-sp-truncation-couple] of $K^\bullet$ for the left exact functor $v=f_*:\Ab(X_{\Et})\to\Ab(Y_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], read through the dictionary [def-sp-etale-dictionary] (so $Rv=Rf_*$):
$$D^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf_*\tau_{\leq q}K),\qquad E^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}\bigl(Rf_*(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q])\bigr),$$
and $(E_r,d_r)_{r\geq2}$ is the spectral sequence of this couple. By [thm-sp-truncation-e2] it is
$$E_2^{p,q}=R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)\Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf_*K),$$
the abutment $\mathcal H^n(Rf_*K)$ carrying the image filtration [def-sp-image-filtration] $F^p\mathcal H^n(Rf_*K)=\operatorname{im}\bigl(\mathcal H^n(Rf_*\tau_{\leq n-p}K)\to\mathcal H^n(Rf_*K)\bigr)$ [def-sp-filtration], finite, with only $a\leq q\leq n$ in total degree $n$, and convergent in the sense of [def-sp-convergence].

2. **Its base change along $g$ (the first sequence of Step 4 of [thm-weil-pbc-bounded-below]).** $g^{-1}(D,E)$ is the couple obtained by applying the exact functor $g^{-1}:\Ab(Y_{\Et})\to\Ab(Y'_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-exact] to every term and structure map of (1). Through the natural isomorphisms $\mathcal H^m(g^{-1}L)\cong g^{-1}\mathcal H^m(L)$ for $L\in\Dplus(Y_{\Et})$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-bounded-below], $g^{-1}$ being the derived inverse image [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], it is the couple obtained by applying $\mathcal H^*$ of the triangulated functor $g^{-1}Rf_*$ to the truncation triangles,
$$D_A^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(g^{-1}Rf_*\tau_{\leq q}K),\qquad E_A^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}\bigl(g^{-1}Rf_*(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q])\bigr),$$
and by [lem-sp-exact-functor-couple] its spectral sequence is $g^{-1}$ applied to that of (1):
$$E_2^{p,q}=g^{-1}R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)\Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(g^{-1}Rf_*K)=g^{-1}\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf_*K),$$
with the filtration $g^{-1}F^p$, which is the image filtration of the maps $\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}Rf_*\tau_{\leq n-p}K)\to\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}Rf_*K)$. This is the sequence called the first spectral sequence wherever the morphism to (3) is formed ([def-weil-pbc-truncation-exact-couples]): it is defined after $g^{-1}$ is applied.

3. **The second truncation spectral sequence (on $Y'$).** $(D',E')$ is the truncation couple of the complex $g'^{-1}K^\bullet$ (terms $g'^{-1}K^i$, zero for $i<a$; it represents $g'^{-1}K$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], has $\tau_{\leq q}(g'^{-1}K^\bullet)=g'^{-1}\tau_{\leq q}K^\bullet$ and $\mathcal H^q(g'^{-1}K)\cong g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)$) for $v=f'_*:\Ab(X'_{\Et})\to\Ab(Y'_{\Et})$:
$$D'^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf'_*g'^{-1}\tau_{\leq q}K),\qquad E'^{p,q}=\mathcal H^{p+q}\bigl(Rf'_*g'^{-1}(\mathcal H^q(K)[-q])\bigr),$$
with spectral sequence, by [thm-sp-truncation-e2],
$$E_2'^{p,q}=R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)\Longrightarrow\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K),$$
the filtration of $\mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K)$ being the image filtration of the maps $\mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}\tau_{\leq n-p}K)\to\mathcal H^n(Rf'_*g'^{-1}K)$, finite with only $a\leq q\leq n$ in degree $n$.

The *hypercohomology filtrations* are the filtrations of the abutments in (1), (2) and (3).

proof.text: Exactness of the cohomological couple. Apply the chosen triangulated functor to each distinguished truncation triangle. Use the three exactness assertions of DerivedCategory.HomologySequence, transport their source and target indices by the displayed equalities, and extract both the zero composites and image-kernel equalities. This proves hypercohomology_maps_exact directly, without importing the raw-complex truncation-couple exactness theorem.

The image filtration is decreasing. For i <= j, factor the inclusion of the truncation at n-j through the truncation at n-i, using the inverse of the smaller truncation inclusion and truncLEMap. Apply the composite Q, the triangulated functor and H^n. The image of a composite is contained in the image of its second factor. This proves hypercohomology_images_antitone.

Lower bounds and stabilization. Transport the given vanishing of H^q(K) to the representing complex. Right derived functors preserve the lower cohomological bound by the source-library isZero_homologyFunctor_rightDerivedFunctorPlus_obj_of_isGE theorem and rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompatibility. Exact derived functors preserve the same bound. A truncation below a is zero in the derived category; a single cohomology object in degree q stays in degrees >= q. Finally the cone of tau<=n K -> K lies in degrees >= n+1, so applying any of the three functors makes its H^n map an isomorphism. These facts give the lower bound for D, the quadrant bound for E and the canonical stabilized abutment map for each sequence.

Convergence with the prescribed filtration. Apply halfPlaneConvergence to each of the three exact couples. The diagonal maps to H^n(FK) are the actual truncation inclusions followed by cohomology. Prove their compatibility and normalize the iterated alpha maps by induction. The map with truncation index n is an isomorphism by the previous step. Apply abutment_image_filtration to identify the finite limiting filtration with the actual images defining hypercohomologyFiltration, including its stated range and all-page vanishing. This uses the general convergence theorem directly rather than the raw-complex truncation hypercohomology theorem.

Bridge and E2 identifications. For the first sequence, conjugate the recorded TruncationCouple.alpha, f and g by the existing bridgeIso, cancel the inverse bridge factors and normalize the cohomological indices. This supplies exactly the three required bridge equations. Identify a single object in degree q with its shift from degree zero, commute the triangulated functor and cohomology with that shift, then use homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso to obtain R^p f_* H^q(K). For the other sequences use the natural exact-functor cohomology comparison and mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor, respectively.

Termwise inverse-image compatibility. An exact additive functor preserves the zero terms and the cohomology of a complex. Construct the truncation comparison with the inverse of the truncation inclusion on the already truncated mapped complex, followed by truncLEMap of the mapped inclusion. Below the truncation degree it is an isomorphism by cancellation; above it both objects are zero. At the top degree, use exactness of the boundary-cycles-homology sequence to show that the cycles map is an isomorphism. Thus the comparison is an isomorphism of complexes and it commutes with the specified inclusions. This proves the existential truncation clause without choosing arbitrary data from an unproved existence statement.

Canonical transport of every page and differential. The fixed mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso gives the comparisons of D and E. Its ordinary naturality gives compatibility with alpha and g; its shift compatibility, followed by naturality for the triangle boundary, gives compatibility with f. Apply exactFunctor_couple to the first couple. Apply coupleMorphism to the resulting comparison and its inverse, and prove by induction that the page maps are inverses, cancelling the cycle inclusion and the epimorphic homology projection at each successor stage. Compose these page isomorphisms with those supplied by exactFunctor_couple. Their page-zero normalization and all differential squares are the ones required in hypercohomologyFiltrations_spec.

Canonical transport of the filtration. Precompose the mapped image inclusion by the mapped epimorphism onto the image; this does not change the image. Replace the resulting composite by the mapped actual abutment map, use naturality of mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso, and cancel its isomorphism on the source. The resulting image is definitionally the second hypercohomology filtration. Combine the finite bounds, convergence, bridge equations, E2 identifications, termwise compatibility and canonical page and filtration comparisons to prove the original specification without changing its statement.

$a$ with $\mathcal H^q(K)=0$ for $q<a$. The canonical truncation tower
$\tau_{\leq q}K$ defines spectral sequences

$$
E_2^{p,q}=R^pf_*\mathcal H^q(K)\Longrightarrow
\mathcal H^{p+q}(Rf_*K),
$$

and

$$
{E'}_2^{p,q}=R^pf'_*g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)\Longrightarrow

$$

proof.text:
The truncation triangles $\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K\to\mathcal
H^q(K)[-q]\to$ are the truncation couple of the spectral-sequence chapter, so
its truncation spectral sequence, applied in the dictionary of that chapter to
the left exact functor $f_*$, supplies the first displayed spectral sequence
with the image filtration, its $E_2$-page being $E_2^{p,q}=R^pf_*\mathcal
H^q(K)$ by the shift identification and the finite-filtration induction. The
second sequence is the same theorem applied to $g'^{-1}K$, exactness of
$g'^{-1}$ giving $\mathcal H^q(g'^{-1}K)=g'^{-1}\mathcal H^q(K)$ and hence the
displayed $E_2'$-page.
